name: Mother Kelly's Bethnal Green
summary: A bottle shop and taproom under the railway arches in Bethnal Green, with a bar lined with beer taps, according to DesignMyNight.

evidence.quote: Mother Kelly's is a bottle shop and taproom nestled underneath the railway arches in Bethnal Green
Kitted out with a bar that showcases a long line of beer taps and a smattering of tables and bar stools
the owners have taken the stripped-back, railway-arch aesthetics applied at their Bethnal Green flagship and recreated them in Vauxhall
The owners have since opened a second venue in Vauxhall along the same lines, with much more space.
The vibe of the place is supposedly inspired by New York craft ale bars

history.change: profile created from the 13 October 2026 venue research
added story: then and one worth-knowing item (Time Out 2017, Londonist 2018)

story.then: The owners later opened a second, roomier branch in Vauxhall, repeating the Bethnal Green original's plain railway-arch style. Time Out called the Bethnal Green bar their flagship.
worth_knowing: Londonist's 2018 entry said the look was supposedly inspired by craft beer bars in New York.

story_research.note: Venue site motherkellys.co.uk and thenudge, CAMRA refused. Found only old press on the Vauxhall sibling link. No opening date, no fresh now/vibe source (DesignMyNight undated). Try Time Out Bethnal Green page, Hackney/Tower Hamlets Slice, Secret London.
